heroHeadline: Goyal Rejects BRICS Currency at Jaipur Trade Talks as NDB Prices $1.75B Bond Ahead of September Summit
heroSubtitle: India's Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal told reporters after chairing the 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' and 10th Industry Ministers' Meetings in Jaipur (Aug 6-7) that 'India is not in favour of a BRICS currency,' a direct on-record rejection weeks before the September 12-13 New Delhi summit. Ministers adopted the Jaipur Consensus on a BRICS Invoice Discounting Mechanism, MSME credit-assessment principles, and a 2026-2030 global-value-chains workplan. India's Department of Personnel and Training separately hosted the final anti-corruption working-group meeting of its chairmanship year in Hyderabad (Aug 4-5), covering fugitive-offender tracing and fintech corruption risks. The New Development Bank priced a $1.75 billion 3-year bond on July 17 (1.8x oversubscribed) and rotated its senior leadership on July 8, reinforcing its funding base ahead of the summit where a further round of accession decisions and the operational BRICS Pay launch are both anticipated.
